textTitles: Saving energy at home: four points of view

texts.title: Saving energy at home: four points of view

paragraphs.text: With energy bills rising, many households are looking for ways to use less. Energy adviser Karen Liu says the cheapest step is to lower the heating by one degree, which most people do not notice but which can cut a heating bill by around ten per cent.

Builder Tom Evans believes insulation matters more than anything else. He points out that in older houses much of the heat escapes through the roof, and that insulating a loft usually pays for itself within three years.

Consumer journalist Sara Mendes warns people to be careful with energy-saving products sold online. She has tested several devices that claim to cut electricity use and found that most made no measurable difference.

The Green Homes Council, a charity, focuses on households that cannot afford improvements. It offers free home visits and small grants, and it has asked the government to fund insulation for low-income families.
Evans adds that people should replace old boilers before spending money on smaller gadgets, while Mendes advises checking independent reviews before buying any new product.
